terms.gloss: believe (a person, a story); believe that, think
evidence: Phaedr. 3.10.1: perīculōsum est crēdere et nōn crēdere
terms.comment: The person or the story believed in the dative (mihi crēde, believe me); what one believes in an accusative and infinitive (tē crēdō surripuisse, I believe you stole it, Phaedr. 1.10.10). Said in passing, crēdō is “I suppose”.

terms.gloss: believe, suppose; opīnor in passing, “I believe”
evidence: Cic. Tusc. 1.92: nōndum, opīnor, est experrēctus

phrases.latin: perīculōsum est crēdere et nōn crēdere
phrases.english: it is dangerous both to believe and not to believe

phrases.latin: crēde mihi, quicquid discis, tibi discis
phrases.english: believe me, whatever you learn, you learn for yourself

phrases.latin: at memoria minuitur. crēdō, nisi eam exerceās
phrases.english: “But memory fades.” I suppose it does, unless you exercise it.

phrases.latin: hanc enim pater sē vīdisse affirmat, puer nōn crēdit
phrases.english: for Dad says he saw the fox; the boy doesn’t believe it

sources: Lewis & Short: credo · Lewis & Short: opinor
